@chapter Introduction #ch-introduction

@section .lede

This field guide collects a season of notes on the birds, insects, and
weather patterns observed from one small backyard. It is meant to be
carried outside, dog-eared, and written in.

@end-section

Most entries below follow the same rhythm: a short observation, the date,
and whatever detail seemed worth keeping. Some notes get expanded later
once a pattern becomes clear across several weeks.

@@callout Getting started

Keep a pencil, not a pen, tucked into the guide's spine. Field notes get
corrected more often than they get finalized, and graphite survives rain
that ink does not.

<div class="tip-box">
  <p>Bring binoculars with at least 8x magnification. Anything weaker
  makes the smaller songbirds indistinguishable from one another at
  typical backyard distances.</p>
</div>

@page-break

The next chapter walks through a full week of entries, showing how the
same short format holds up whether the day was eventful or quiet.
